problem: The counselor gate is documented as a human trust boundary but is computed from client-supplied draft body fields (match.gaps, match.biasAlerts, match.transport.feasible, evidence[].credentialStatus). It is both bypassable by a crafted body and, for honest callers, blind because the counterfactual auditor never runs on the UI match path.

caseA_bypass.assertion: clean body yields counselorGate == [] and submit reaches pending_employer_approval with no counselor approval

caseB_missing.assertion: trusted decision with a critical gap forces counselorGate to contain critical_gap

honestBlindness: apps/agent-runtime/src/matching/adapt.ts:107 projects biasAlerts from the vacancy document
evidence.existingTrustedSeam: apps/agent-runtime/src/application/shortlist.ts ShortlistSource (ownerOf, match) already recomputes via SQL + solver + counterfactual auditor

decision.recommendation: Widen and rename the existing trusted seam ShortlistSource -> ApplicationDecisionSource, and make the counselor gate consume it instead of the request body.

interface.decisionFor: decisionFor(candidateId: string, vacancyId: string): Promise<{ decision?: MatchDecision; biasBlocked: boolean }>

callerObligations: ownership comes only from ownerOf; a body value is never authoritative
decisionFor is authoritative and may return no decision; absence is not success
absence fails closed: never create a draft with an empty gate when the trusted decision is unavailable
hiddenBehindSeam: Postgres-backed profile and preference reads via SqlQuery
counterfactual auditor passes over protected attributes
bias alert derivation from the auditor rather than the vacancy document

depthAnalysis.deletionTest: Deleting the seam scatters profile loading, solver re-run, counterfactual audit, alert derivation, ownership resolution and the fail-closed rule across every caller.
depthAnalysis.locality: Concentrates the trust rule for aptitude, gaps, alerts and transport in one module; ownership trust already lives there after the draft-employer-org fix.
depthAnalysis.leverage: One adapter serves createDraft, the counselor queue, the employer shortlist and the bias audit trail.
depthAnalysis.mainCost: createDraft must become asynchronous because the trusted decision requires I/O.

alternatives.summary: Run the auditor on the UI match path, keep the body as the gate source
alternatives.why: fixes honest blindness but leaves the gate client-controlled; pays counterfactual cost per page view

alternatives.summary: Sign the decision in the BFF and verify it in the runtime
alternatives.why: adds key management and a trust token without settling who may decide

alternatives.summary: Widen the existing trusted seam and consume it in the gate
alternatives.why: reuses the seam whose contract already forbids body-sourced truth

alternatives.summary: Evaluate the gate only at submit time
alternatives.why: the draft view and counselor queue would show an untrusted gate while claiming otherwise

acceptanceCriteria: A trusted critical gap, unverified credential, bias alert or infeasible transport always produces the matching counselorGate code, whatever the body claims
A body claiming a clean match cannot clear a trusted gate
An unresolvable trusted decision either blocks draft creation or forces the gate; never an empty gate
submit still refuses without counselor approval when a trusted gate exists, and the counselor queue lists exactly the gated drafts
Ownership resolution is unchanged from the current behaviour
migrationSlices: Widen and rename the seam with no observable behaviour change
Make createDraft async, resolve ownership plus decision through the seam, force the gate on unresolved decisions; update server.ts:116 dispatch and direct callers
Remove or demote the body-sourced match to an advisory echo that cannot influence the gate
Add the regression tests for the acceptance criteria
openQuestion: In memory mode there is no persisted profile and therefore no trusted decision: either refuse draft creation (503, matching shortlist_unavailable) or force the counselor gate for every draft. The ADR must settle this.
